newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis jumps after Sudan deal report.
newsitem.headline: Arakis jumps after Sudan deal report.

text.p: Investors rushed to grab shares of Canadian oil company Arakis Energy Corp on Tuesday after the company revealed it was drawing close to a possible deal with joint venture partners for the development of its oil concession in Sudan.
Arakis, by far the most active stock on Nasdaq, climbed 3/4 to 4, on more than 17 million shares. The stock has been active since Friday.
Arakis chief executive John Mcleod told Reuters on Monday that a deal involving international oil companies could be announced in 30 days.

The company is in discussions with at least three companies, which sources said included firms based in Europe and the United States, with the aim of signing a deal that could see one or more take a stake in Arakis's Heglig and Unity fields in southern Sudan and a 900-mile pipeline to be built to the Red Sea from the fields.
The estimated cost of developing the fields and pipeline is US$930 million, to be spent over 30 months.
The company has attempted to strike a conventional joint venture deal since a highly publicized US$750-million financing for a pipeline fell through last year.

McLeod said on Monday that a key hurdle for the company was cleared in August when the U.S. government ruled that Sudan was not subject to broad U.S. trade and investment sanctions under its anti-terrorism law.
The move opened the door to the potential entrance of U.S.-based companies into the deal.
